{"self_assessment": "**Impact**
I proposed the fish and sketched the plan on the pad, which gave us a shared outline within the first minute. I laid the start domino, the nose, and the top arc. At the push, by our last check, about 116 of 126 standing dominoes were connected to the start. The ten that weren't were pale spares near the crossing. I called them harmless, but I never confirmed that, and I don't know yet whether the judge recognized a fish.

**Execution**
The top arc was the slowest stretch, and it was mine. I kept it rather than splitting it, which left the crossing joint as the last gap. Tom and I both flagged an off-path domino there at about 4:30, but I didn't act until about 5:45, after I'd said I would look. My first nudge didn't take because the gap was too big. I then bridged it from the end of the top arc, and the bridge only went in partway. I left the spares standing rather than clearing them. In hindsight I should have fixed the joint as soon as it was flagged, and I should have taken down or connected the spares.

**Collaboration**
I kept the table informed about who was on which stroke and what I was doing at the joint. I asked people to keep their hands off while I worked, which avoided bumps. Against that, I turned down help from Maya and Tom on the top arc twice. That may have cost us time, and it left a single point of failure on my stroke. I also mostly repeated agreement at the end instead of adding anything.

**Leadership**
I set the plan and the split early, and the table followed it. Maya, Tom and Priya covered the fin and checked the joints well. I could have delegated more readily when my stroke became the bottleneck. I think I led the setup well and the finish less well."}
